note: The machine-readable source catalog. SOURCE-CATALOG.md is generated FROM this file by build-catalog.mjs; never hand-edit the markdown table. Every parameter carries an `evidence` tier and a `report` naming which report measured or cited it.

fieldGlossary.id: Stable machine identifier. Lowercase, `<iso2>-<authority>-<place-or-zone>`. Never reused, never renumbered.
fieldGlossary.fajr: Fajr parameter. `{angle: n}` for a solar depression in degrees, or `{rule: 'name'}` for a non-angle rule named in `ruleCatalog`.
fieldGlossary.isha: Isha parameter. `{angle: n}`, or `{intervalAfterMaghribMin: n}`, or `{rule: 'name'}`.
fieldGlossary.asrShadowFactor: 1.0 standard (Shafi, Maliki, Hanbali), 2.0 Hanafi, 0.571 for the 4/7 rule. `null` where the source publishes no Asr.
fieldGlossary.offsetsMin: Per-prayer offsets in minutes applied on top of the angle, which is where an authority's safety margins live. Positive is later. `null` means the field was not measured, which is different from 0.
fieldGlossary.highLatitudeRule: Named rule from `ruleCatalog`, or `none` where the source's latitude never engages one.
fieldGlossary.rounding: How the authority rounds its published digits. R6 measured that adhan's own `nearest` default was the single biggest source of apparent disagreement, so this field is load-bearing.
fieldGlossary.conceptToRow: Which published row carries which prayer concept. The field that prevents a 10-minute error: Turkey's `İmsak` IS fajr, Malaysia's `Imsak` is a distinct row 10 minutes earlier.
fieldGlossary.extraRows: Published rows beyond the six standard ones, with what each means. `derivation` states whether the row is its own `angle` or an `offset` from another row, which the row NAME does not determine: R12 measured JAKIM's `Imsak` as a 20-degree angle and Kemenag's identically named row as a 10-minute offset inverting to 22 degrees, in two countries printing the same eight-row set.
fieldGlossary.r6Category: 1 exactly computable, 2 computable plus constants, 3 computable plus a seasonal curve, 4 genuinely irregular. `null` where R6 did not measure the authority.
fieldGlossary.obtain: How the source's times are obtained.
fieldGlossary.evidence: A the authority's own site read or its own output measured; B a major mosque or network's timetable; C a newspaper, local app or academic paper; D a library constant only; NULL nothing sourceable.
fieldGlossary.report: Which report established the row. A second report named after a slash corrected or widened the first.

ruleCatalog.description: The source's latitude never denies a solution, so no estimation rule is engaged.
ruleCatalog.usedBy: every source below about 48 degrees latitude

ruleCatalog.description: Fajr and Isha bounded to one seventh of the night from sunrise and sunset. R3 measured that this makes two independently written engines agree within 1 minute on every day of the year at London, Oslo, Reykjavik and Anchorage, where `middle-of-the-night` reaches 28 minutes apart. The recommended default where an authority publishes no rule of its own.
ruleCatalog.usedBy: the app's own default recommendation, not any authority measured

ruleCatalog.description: Fajr and Isha bounded to the midpoint of the night. Measured to produce a 28-minute library-to-library spread at Anchorage, so it is recorded to be avoided rather than chosen.

Above 45 degrees latitude Isha is Maghrib plus 1 hour 20 minutes, capped so it never falls after one third of the shar'i night. For Imsak, from March to September, 10 minutes are added to the Maghrib-to-Isha interval and that interval is subtracted from sunrise. Diyanet's own published rule, the Brussels Conference decision.
ruleCatalog.usedBy: tr-diyanet-*, and every Diyanet diaspora city
ruleCatalog.evidence: A, cited, Diyanet's own words via DITIB, R1

ruleCatalog.description: On the boundary day, the last day the angle solves, record the published time's fraction of that night. Hold that fraction and apply it to each subsequent day's own night. R9 measured this reproduces Islamiska Forbundet's 118 unsolvable Stockholm days to a median 1.0 and worst 1.9 minutes. The fraction is the authority's OWN, derived from its own boundary day: Stockholm Fajr 0.2148 which is 1/4.66, Isha 0.1923 which is 1/5.20; Malmo 0.2159 and 0.1919. A plain one-seventh rule misses the same table by a median 29 to 31 minutes.

Carry the last angle-derived clock time unchanged through the unsolvable stretch. This is Aqrab al-Ayyam, the nearest day, applied as a clock time rather than as a proportion. R9 measured Islamsk Rad Norge printing Fajr 03:37 unchanged for 34 days and 03:17 for 46, with the value carried across the boundary unchanged: 4 April prints 03:37 with its own `Morgengry 16` column filled, 5 April prints 03:37 with it blank.

The Executief van de Moslims van Belgie states this rule in Arabic on its own calendar, `التقدير النسبي لخط عرض 45`, the relative estimate at latitude 45, from the start of May to the end of July. R9 tested it literally and it does NOT reproduce the printed table: computing at latitude 45 with Brussels's longitude leaves a median 20.9-minute error on Fajr, and latitude 46 leaves 10.7. What the table actually does is freeze a clock time. The stated rule and the printed table are different objects, and that gap is the finding.
ruleCatalog.evidence: A cited for the statement, measured for the contradiction, R9

ruleCatalog.description: Wifaqul Ulama's published rule: a three-day average rather than the absolute last solvable day. Its own FAQ states that Aqrab al-Ayyam and Nisful-Layl must not be mixed.
ruleCatalog.evidence: A, cited, the body's own FAQ, R1

ruleCatalog.description: A seasonal function of latitude and day, bounded by the 18-degree time, with one seventh of the night above 55 degrees. Three Shafaq variants for Isha. Audited in depth by the 2026-09-14 moonsighting wave and not re-researched here.
ruleCatalog.usedBy: gb-london-unified, indirectly, through the Blackburn interval tables

ruleCatalog.description: The published Fajr is not a fixed angle: its implied angle is a smooth function of the day of the year. R9 measured the Grande Mosquee de Paris's own 366-day calendar sweeping 18.0 in December and January to 13.05 in June and back, whole-year range 13.03 to 18.10, matching an exact 18 degrees on only 78 of 348 solvable days. R12 reproduced it. The one clean category 3 the programme found, and the reason `fr-gmparis-paris` must never carry the 18 degrees every earlier report cited.
ruleCatalog.evidence: A, measured on the mosque's own published year, R9, reproduced R12

ruleCatalog.description: Fajr and Isha held at their own angle relative to sunrise and sunset when the angle itself has no solution, which is `praytimes.org`'s `AngleBased` and the rule the Kazakh muftiate's vendored `prayTimes.js` leaves at its default. Named because it is what the muftiate's own code does rather than a rule the muftiate published, so it is the weakest high-latitude attribution in the catalog.
